_doc: Ground-truth corpora for the Argus Phase 10 citation check and for grounded drafting. This file MIRRORS the built-in set in src/corpus.ts (BUILT_IN_CORPORA) — both corpora, verbatim. Copy it to data/corpora.json and edit from there. Absent = the built-in set. Lives in docs/ because data/*.json is gitignored, and that rule keeps live session cookies out of the repository.
_this_file_replaces_it_wholesale: loadConfigs() in src/corpus.ts returns THIS ARRAY INSTEAD OF the built-in set the moment data/corpora.json exists. There is no merge and there is no warning. A copy that drops wordpress-primary drops the only corpus with draftable:true, and grounded drafting stops finding anything — silently, with no error, because 'no reference material for this subject' is the honest and common answer for a narrow corpus and is indistinguishable from 'the corpus is gone'. That is why this example ships both entries rather than one: it is a starting point to edit, not a fragment to paste.
_principle: A corpus has a jurisdiction — the claims it is entitled to rule on — and it is silent everywhere else. Silence is recorded as silence, never as approval. Adjudicating and drafting are separate permissions: see `rules` and `draftable` below.
_why_so_narrow: Measured 2026-07-24 against the real SGEN KB (3,544 cards): 17 mention WordPress and every one of them says 'SGEN does not do that'; 2 mention mysql; updraft, elementor, woocommerce and jquery score zero. redbot answers WordPress questions, so ruling on WordPress claims with that corpus would flag ~100% of them — and a flag that is almost always true is not a filter (DEFECT-15). What it CAN rule on is claims about SGEN, and a fabricated product capability asserted in a public subreddit is unretractable. wordpress-primary exists to cover the handful of technical subjects redbot actually argues about, and its jurisdiction is derived from the cards it holds, not from the domain — a corpus that claimed 'WordPress' generally would put nearly every claim in jurisdiction, hold nothing on most of them, and reject them.

_fields.id: stable identifier, cited in verdict reasons
_fields.label: how to name it in operator-facing prose — it appears in review packages
_fields.path: path to the JSON file; relative paths resolve from the repo root. The corpus may live outside this repository.
_fields.cardsAt: dotted path to the array of cards inside that JSON; empty string means the file IS the array
_fields.fields: which card properties carry the id, the question and the body
_fields.require: field/value pairs a card must match to be usable at all
_fields.jurisdiction: claim-text regex sources that put a claim inside this corpus's authority. A claim matching none of these is not ruled on.
_fields.rules: OPTIONAL, DEFAULTS TO TRUE — omitting it grants STANDING. A corpus with standing can turn `uncited` into a REJECT through Argus Rule 9, so a thin corpus added without thinking about this field becomes a handbrake on its whole jurisdiction. Set it to false to add a corpus for retrieval only: it is then invisible to Phases 9/10/11 and cannot reject, escalate or certify anything.
_fields.draftable: OPTIONAL, DEFAULTS TO FALSE — omitting it means the corpus is NEVER read while drafting a public reply. Opting in is explicit because the cost of the wrong corpus here is a reply that drifts toward whatever the corpus is about. The two flags are independent: sgen-kb rules but is not drafted from, wordpress-primary is drafted from but does not rule.
_fields.note: free text, shown to an operator alongside the corpus

corpora.label: the SGEN knowledge base
corpora.note: Human-authored support cards about the SGEN product. Jurisdiction is claims about SGEN only — it knows nothing about WordPress and does not pretend to. `require` excludes the 56 INTERNAL cards on purpose: a citation check that reads internal material can surface it in a review package that gets pasted somewhere. It also excludes source-only cards, leaving 3,414 of 3,544. `rules` and `draftable` are both omitted, which is the pair of defaults this corpus wants: full standing to adjudicate, never read while drafting, because retrieving product cards to answer a WordPress question is the exact signal config.brand.forbidMention exists to suppress.

corpora.label: WordPress and MySQL primary documentation
corpora.note: Eight cards of quoted primary documentation (dev.mysql.com, developer.wordpress.org). This is the corpus grounded drafting reads from — the only one with draftable:true — so removing it from a copy of this file turns grounded drafting off. `rules: false` was set on evidence, not caution: replayed over all 216 logged claims on 2026-07-27 it put 194 out of jurisdiction, 6 `covered` and 16 `uncited`, and reading those 16 by hand found about five correct kills against eleven TRUE claims that simply clear no card at the 0.5 term-coverage bar. A gate that rejects more true claims than false ones is not a gate. It earns standing later, on coverage. Each jurisdiction pattern names a subject a card actually covers; src/test/corpus-standing.test.ts fails if any of them matches no card.

_two_rules_that_are_not_negotiable: HUMAN-AUTHORED ONLY. Never point a corpus at model output — feeding Argus's own refutations back as ground truth is a model writing its own answer key, which is HRC-001 one level up. Two wordpress-primary cards state facts Argus derived adversarially and a human reviewer missed, and they are held on the authority of the published sources they quote, never on Argus's.

A MATCH IS NOT AGREEMENT. Retrieval is deterministic term overlap, so it finds cards ABOUT a subject and cannot tell one that confirms a claim from one that refutes it. Measured 2026-07-24: the false claim 'SGEN supports installing WordPress plugins' matched kb-can-i-install-a-plugin at 0.60 coverage — the card that says the opposite. That outcome is reported as `covered` and escalates to a person with the cards attached; it never certifies.
